We carefully chose a set of models that were maximally distinct from each other, offering us the widest range and variability of generated text. We focused on varying model sizes, open/closed source, and chat/completion style. Following work by Sarvazyan et al. (2023a), we select largest model from each model family and exclude third-party fine-tuned variants of base models in favor of the base models themselves. candidate_windows.section_title: experiments on multilingual and code generations (raid-extra)
candidate_windows.normalized_section_title: experiments on multilingual and code generations (raid-extra)
candidate_windows.window_text: In addition to the main RAID dataset we also release RAID-Extra: a collection of 2.3M generations in three extra challenging domains: Python Code, Czech News, and German News. These extra experiments were not included in the main benchmark as we felt that they were out of scope for most detectors and should not be used as a basis for comparison. Nonetheless, we were still curious to see what sorts of insights they can give us on detector performance.

We ran our generations over the course of 15 days from November 1st 2023 to November 15th 2023 on 32 NVIDIA 48GB A6000 GPUs. We ran all models with 16-bit precision as we found that outputs were identical to full precision and it cut our inference time in half. The amount of GPU hours used by each family of models is as follows: LLaMA 2 70B (+ Chat) 8,376 hours, MPT (+ Chat) 5,440 hours, Mistral (+ Chat) 672 hours, GPT2 (+ Chat) 352 hours. In total we used 14,872 GPU hours (620 GPU days) to generate the RAID dataset.
